competitors.name: KnowBe4
competitors.entry_point: Users tab → select user → Assign Admin Functions; or Security Roles tab → create role → attach groups
competitors.setup_friction: Base roles (Account Owner, Full Admin, Group Admin) require no setup. Security Roles require creating a named role, attaching groups, and configuring permission toggles — available on Advanced/Platinum/Diamond tiers only
core_flow: Navigate to Users tab or Security Roles tab
Select user or create new role
Assign role (base tier) or configure permission toggles (Security Roles)
competitors.error_prevention: Additive permissions model — multiple roles stack, permissions are never removed by adding a second role
competitors.trust_model: Admin-only role creation. No self-serve escalation path.
competitors.rbac_notes: Three fixed roles plus custom Security Roles layer (tier-gated). Group Admin is scoped to assigned groups — data filtered at query level, not separate UI. Permissions are additive across groups.
competitors.repeat_use_efficiency: Security Roles creation is reusable — create once, attach to any group. Group Admins are role-scoped by group membership, which updates dynamically.
competitors.source_notes: Role model observed via Stitchflow user management guide and public KnowBe4 blog post on delegated permissions. Security Roles UI specifics are inferred from documentation structure, not direct product observation.

competitors.name: Adaptive Security
competitors.entry_point: Admin portal → Admin Access section → Add an Admin (new) or three-dot menu → Change Role (existing)
competitors.setup_friction: Low — six fixed roles, no custom role configuration required
core_flow: Navigate to Admin Access in admin portal
Click 'Add an Admin' or open three-dot menu on existing user
Select role from fixed list of six
feedback_states: Role change via three-dot menu — immediate effect inferred
competitors.error_prevention: Only Account Owners and Team Admins can modify roles — prevents accidental escalation by scoped users
competitors.trust_model: Owner and Team Admin only can assign roles. No self-serve escalation path observed.
competitors.rbac_notes: Six functional roles: Account Owner, Team Admin, Training Manager, Content Manager, Phishing Manager, Report Viewer. Training and Phishing are separate roles — unlike Dune's bundle. Report Viewer is a first-class read-only role.
competitors.repeat_use_efficiency: Fixed role set requires no setup — role assignment is a one-step action per user
competitors.source_notes: Role names and assignment flow observed from Adaptive Security product blog post announcing RBAC. Permission boundaries within each role are inferred from role descriptions.

competitors.name: Proofpoint SAT
competitors.setup_friction: Module-level toggles per role — requires admin to configure each module's visibility per role type
core_flow: User-level override takes priority over global settings
feedback_states: User-level override documented — global defaults can be overridden per user
competitors.error_prevention: User-level access control overrides global — prevents global setting changes from accidentally locking out specific users
competitors.trust_model: Admin-configured via settings panel. No self-serve escalation.
competitors.rbac_notes: Named tiers: Super Admin, Training Admin, User Admin. Read-only admin user is a first-class role in Proofpoint Essentials. 5 roles with customizable module toggles.
competitors.repeat_use_efficiency: Module toggles are persistent — configure once per role tier
competitors.source_notes: Role names from training course materials and Proofpoint Essentials admin guide. UI flow for role assignment, confirmation states, and dashboard scoping are inferred, not directly observed.

competitors.name: Hoxhunt
competitors.entry_point: Admin portal — specific RBAC entry point not documented publicly
competitors.setup_friction: SCIM provisioning supported — role attributes mapped from IdP (Microsoft Entra ID documented)
core_flow: Multi-tenant Admin has cross-org access to Admin Portal and Insights
competitors.trust_model: Multi-tenant model with Owner Organization admin controlling cross-org access
competitors.rbac_notes: Primary documented model is multi-tenancy. Single-tenant role granularity is sparse in public docs.
competitors.repeat_use_efficiency: SCIM ensures role sync stays current without manual updates
competitors.source_notes: Most RBAC documentation is behind authentication. SCIM support confirmed via Microsoft Learn provisioning tutorial. Role granularity for single-tenant accounts is inferred.

observed_patterns: Functional role names (Training Manager, Phishing Manager, Report Viewer) over permission-level labels
User-first role assignment via context menu or user row action
Scoped dashboard data filtered at query level — same UI surface across roles
Read-only as a first-class named role, not an implied state
SCIM provisioning supported by all enterprise-tier competitors
Fixed role sets for standard deployments; custom role builders for enterprise tiers
anti_patterns: Role-first assignment flow (create role → attach groups → configure permissions) adds unnecessary abstraction for small fixed role sets
Hiding gated nav items without first-login onboarding leaves scoped users assuming setup is broken
'Contact your admin' dead-end at permission-denied state with no structured access request path
Additive permission stacking (KnowBe4) creates hard-to-predict permission states in multi-group scenarios
Session behavior on role change is universally undocumented — a security gap across the category
differentiation_opportunities: AEP as a first-class named surface in the role model signals AI personalization differentiation at the permission layer
Role-change warning when user has an active campaign — no competitor surfaces this explicitly
In-product access request flow from the permission-denied state — unmet need across the category
First-login role onboarding modal or banner to surface permission boundaries — absent from all competitors reviewed
Explicit audit log UI accessible to Full Access admins — treat role history as a trust signal, not just a compliance log
design_implications: Build role × surface × action type state matrix before any Figma work begins
Use user-first role assignment (inline selector on user row) — not role-first configuration screen
Design dashboard as a single component with role-scoped data — do not build separate dashboard UIs per role
Add an action to the permission-denied empty state — at minimum a 'Request access' CTA
Plan for SCIM in v1 scope or explicitly defer it and define the bulk onboarding workaround
Add first-login role awareness banner or modal for scoped users
confidence_notes: KnowBe4 and Adaptive Security role models are high confidence from public documentation
Proofpoint SAT is medium confidence — role names confirmed but UI flow is inferred
Hoxhunt is low confidence for RBAC specifics — documentation is mostly behind authentication
No competitor's permission-denied UX, session invalidation behavior, or dashboard scoping visuals were directly observed
